anya: Heads-up: console is showing negative per-model savings for some sessions. I dug into it and it looks like cache savings are being double-counted when sessions are sticky but the router falls back mid-session. sample below where unit econ goes negative :thinking:

miguel: can you paste a minimal repro? my guess: we apply prefetch credits at billing time, but when session attribution shifts on reroute the credits end up applied to tokens that didn’t actually consume the prefetch.

anya: repro snippet: session started on route=eu-west with model=gpt-lite, prefetch_kv=120 at warmup, then router fell back to gpt-small for the last 40 tokens. console shows the prefetch credit applied across all 160 tokens.

anya: ```
session_id=abc123
start_route=eu-west
start_model=gpt-lite
prefetch_kv_count=120
total_tokens=160
fallback_model=gpt-small
fallback_tokens=40
```

lina: do we have the router metadata needed so billing can do per-token allocation? we added a route_handoff event earlier but maybe it lacks token offsets.

miguel: router emits route_handoff with session_id + timestamp, but it only reports prefetch_kv at initial warmup. we don’t currently emit the number of prefetch-consumed tokens or a token index at handoff. that’s the gap.

product-sam: UX asks: 1) display adjusted per-model unit-econ with a small confidence/sample-size badge, and 2) add a "why negative" drilldown that lists routing handoffs and attribution metadata so PMs/support can trace it.

anya: billing-side quick fix proposal: when we see a handoff event, allocate prefetch_kv_cost pro-rata to tokens before the handoff_token_index, and do not apply prefetch credits to tokens after the handoff.

miguel: algorithmically fine, but requires a canonical token ordering for the session. two ways: router emits periodic token_offset markers (every N tokens, N=32), or emit a single handoff_token_index at the moment of handoff.

lina: emitting handoff_token_index is much smaller blast radius. router adds fields in telemetry: handoff_token_index and prefetch_kv. then billing can join usage by token index.

anya: note: some legacy dedicated routers might not support extra fields. fallback for them: billing estimates handoff index using timestamps + average tokens/sec heuristics. we'll mark those allocations as "estimated" in the console.

product-sam: UX detail: for canary rollouts and cost previews, show an error badge e.g. "est. ±12% (heuristic)" and allow toggling between provisional and reconciled numbers once billing jobs finish.

miguel: architecture debate: should router emit headers on requests (x-handoff-token-index) for sync consumption by billing, or emit an async telemetry event? headers are immediate but couple router to billing semantics; events keep router dumb and let attribution evolve.

lina: i prefer telemetry events. router remains thin and we can evolve attribution logic centrally. downside is eventual consistency in console metrics. but we already surface reconciled vs provisional in other panels.

anya: agreed: plan = router emits session_handoff event with {session_id, handoff_token_index, prefetch_kv}. telemetry indexes to session-attribution table; billing joins tokenized usage to that table for final allocation; console shows provisional numbers and reconciled marker once billing job runs.

sre-bot: deploy-bot: canary deploy started for router-prefetch-metadata -> 3/5 hosts updated :rocket:

miguel: console UX: add a tiny timeline sparkline per session overlaying route spans so users can visually see where credits were applied. also include a tooltip that shows raw metadata (prefetch_kv, handoff_index, event_ids) for support handoff.

lina: implementation checklist: router: emit session_handoff telemetry event; telemetry: index into session-attribution table; billing: nightly reconciliation join job; console: show provisional vs reconciled and add drilldown + error badges.

anya: timeline: router + telemetry indexing = 2d, billing join + nightly job = 3d, console UX + toggle = 2d. can ship phased behind a feature flag, with P0 focus on preventing negative savings affecting top 10 tenants panel.

product-sam: i’ll add details to rollout doc and schedule a quick UX review before we flip the FF. can someone file a tiny integration test for the billing join?

anya: i'll open a PR with example vectors and attach to the rollout doc. :thumbsup:

miguel: reassigning to eng-platform to track infra work.

lina: i’ll write a short runbook for support explaining provisional vs reconciled numbers and how to collect the handoff event ids.

anya: thanks all, closing when PR lands. :eyes:
